blocks.source: 【作曲講座】伴奏（コード進行）を作る
blocks.translation: [Composition Guide] Creating an Accompaniment (Chord Progression)

blocks.source: 主旋律の次に伴奏を作成します。同時にコード進行も決まります。
blocks.translation: Next, create the accompaniment. The chord progression will be determined at the same time.

blocks.source: トラックを『CH02』に変更します。
blocks.translation: Change the track to “CH02.”

blocks.source: 楽器は初期値だとピアノになっています。ピアノは伴奏によく使われるので、そのままでもいけないことはないです。でも、フィールドっぽくしたいならば49～52番のStrings系かなと。とにかく、好みのものを選択してください。
blocks.translation: The instrument is initially set to piano. Piano is often used for accompaniment, so there is nothing wrong with leaving it as is. However, if you want a field-like sound, I would suggest something in the Strings range, numbers 49–52. In any case, choose whichever you prefer.

blocks.source: オニオンスキン
blocks.translation: Onion Skin

blocks.source: 伴奏は先に作った主旋律に合わせて作るので、主旋律を見ながら作りたいところ。そこでDominoのオニオンスキン機能を使用します。
blocks.translation: Since the accompaniment is created to match the previously created melody, it is helpful to be able to see the melody while working. To do this, use Domino’s onion skin feature.

blocks.source: オニオンスキンというのは、編集中以外のトラックの音符も薄く表示してくれる機能です。設定方法はこの辺を参照してください。
blocks.translation: Onion skin is a feature that displays the notes of tracks other than the one being edited in a lighter color. See here for instructions on how to configure it.

blocks.source: http://mimikopi.nomaki.jp/midi/002/trackselect/#C05
blocks.translation: http://mimikopi.nomaki.jp/midi/002/trackselect/#C05

blocks.source: これで主旋律を参照しながら打ち込めるようになりました。
blocks.translation: Now you can enter notes while referring to the melody.

blocks.source: 伴奏は主旋律と『不協和音』をなるべく起こさないように打ち込んでいきます。とりあえず一小節をまるまる使う『全音符』で打ち込みます。理由は何も考えないのでよいので楽だから。
blocks.translation: Enter the accompaniment while trying to avoid creating “dissonance” with the melody as much as possible. For now, enter it using “whole notes,” which fill an entire measure. This is because it is easy—you do not have to think about anything.

blocks.source: 三和音を作る
blocks.translation: Creating Triads

blocks.source: 僕が作成中の曲を例に挙げます。最初の一小節目、主旋律は「ラド」となっていますね。
blocks.translation: I’ll use the song I’m currently creating as an example. In the first measure, the melody is “La Do,” isn’t it?

blocks.source: なので、伴奏もラとドを含む『三和音』にします。『和音』にするためには『不協和音』を避ける必要があります。隣り合った音「ドとレ」「ドとシ」「ラとシ」「ラとソ」などが不協和音となります。
blocks.translation: Therefore, make the accompaniment a “triad” that includes La and Do as well. To make a “chord,” you need to avoid “dissonance.” Adjacent notes such as “Do and Re,” “Do and Ti,” “La and Ti,” and “La and Sol” create dissonance.

blocks.source: ※実は四和音になると不協和音も含むようになります。しかし、複雑にしないため、及びそもそも筆者があまり詳しくないのであえて割愛します。興味ある方はググってください。
blocks.translation: ※Actually, when a chord has four notes, it can also include dissonance. However, I’ll leave that out intentionally, both to avoid making things complicated and because I’m not very knowledgeable about the subject to begin with. If you’re interested, search online.

blocks.source: 実は不協和音にならない選択肢は「ドミラ」と「ドファラ」しかなかったりします。今回は「ドファラ」にしてみました。この組み合わせが『コード進行』そのものです。
blocks.translation: In fact, the only options that do not create dissonance are “Do Mi La” and “Do Fa La.” This time, I tried “Do Fa La.” This combination itself is the “chord progression.”

blocks.source: 別に「ラドファ」でも「ファラド」でもよいです。音の組み合わせが大事なので、上下を変えてもＯＫです。選択肢は限られていますが、それぞれ印象は結構変わってくるので、色々と演奏しながら試してください。
blocks.translation: “La Do Fa” or “Fa La Do” would be fine too. The combination of notes is what matters, so changing their order is OK. Although the options are limited, each one creates a considerably different impression, so try various combinations while playing them.

blocks.source: さて、問題は二小節目。主旋律が「シソラ」になってますね。シとソとラを合わせたら、どう考えても不協和音にしかなりません。しょうがないので適当にごまかします。実のところ、全く不協和音を出さないというのは不可能ですが、ちょっとぐらいなら大丈夫です。
blocks.translation: Now, the problem is the second measure. The melody is “Ti Sol La,” isn’t it? Combining Ti, Sol, and La can only result in dissonance, no matter how you look at it. So I’ll just fudge it somehow. In reality, it is impossible to avoid dissonance completely, but a little is fine.

blocks.source: とりあえず、小節の出だしの音（ここではシ）は目立つので和音に含めておいたほうが無難です。「シミソ」か「シレソ」辺りでいいんでないでしょうか。もちろん「ミソシ」や「レソシ」も同じです。
blocks.translation: For now, it is safer to include the note at the beginning of the measure (Ti here) in the chord, since it stands out. “Ti Mi Sol” or “Ti Re Sol” should work. Of course, “Mi Sol Ti” and “Re Sol Ti” are the same.

blocks.source: という感じで伴奏も３２小節まで埋めていってください。数は多いですが、選択肢は限られていますので、半機械的にちゃっちゃとやっていきましょう。
blocks.translation: Continue filling in the accompaniment up to the 32nd measure in this way. There are many of them, but the options are limited, so let’s get through them fairly mechanically and quickly.

blocks.source: 伴奏も主旋律と同じでコピペ技が使えます。
blocks.translation: Just like with the melody, you can use copy and paste for the accompaniment.

blocks.source: こんな感じになりました。伴奏は三和音なのでそのままだと少し音が大きいです。音量（Volume）を主旋律よりも下げてます。適当に調整してみてください。
blocks.translation: This is what it looks like now. Since the accompaniment consists of triads, it sounds a little loud as is. I lowered the volume (Volume) below that of the melody. Try adjusting it as appropriate.

blocks.source: TestField_Accompaniment_1.mid
blocks.translation: TestField_Accompaniment_1.mid

blocks.source: 面倒なので後のキャプチャは貼りません。気になるなら、DominoでMIDIを読み込んで中を見てください。何気に作曲ソフトがMIDIを直接読み込めるのって、結構凄いことなんですよね。昔はそんなことができるソフトは希少でした。
blocks.translation: I won’t include any more screenshots because it’s tedious. If you’re curious, load the MIDI into Domino and take a look inside. It’s actually quite impressive that music composition software can load MIDI files directly. In the past, software capable of doing that was rare.

blocks.source: 刻む
blocks.translation: Adding Rhythmic Notes

blocks.source: 一応できました。……が、このままでは面白みがない感じです。
blocks.translation: It’s done, for the most part. …But as it is, it feels a little uninteresting.

blocks.source: 試しに最初の１６小節は全音符をやめてみましょうか。「４分音符→４分休符→４分音符→４分休符」の構成にしてみます。
blocks.translation: Let’s try replacing the whole notes in the first 16 measures. We’ll use the structure “quarter note → quarter rest → quarter note → quarter rest.”

blocks.source: 後ろの１６小節は全音符のままのほうが雰囲気が出そうなのでそのままです。
blocks.translation: The latter 16 measures are left as whole notes because they seem to create a better atmosphere that way.

blocks.source: これでかなりそれっぽくなりました。最初の１６小節と後ろの１６小節で雰囲気がいい感じに変わります。
blocks.translation: Now it sounds much more like what we were aiming for. The mood changes nicely between the first 16 measures and the latter 16 measures.

blocks.source: TestField_Accompaniment_2.mid
blocks.translation: TestField_Accompaniment_2.mid
